page: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is a virtual instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz under the QEMU hypervisor. The instance provisions 8 shared vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 1 thread per core, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI for accelerated cryptographic and vector computations. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 1.95 GB per vCPU, alongside 320 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the cpx42 with strong single-threaded performance, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2,991.79 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 14.1 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of measured systems. In contrast, multi-core metrics reflect average tier execution, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 23,749.36, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 9,475.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 19,462.24. Throughput tests record 13.06 GB/sec in static web serving and 19.57 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads. Small-scale model inference registers 297.53 tokens per second for 135M parameter text generation, while medium 7B models yield 24.88 tokens per second.

The shared CPU allocation model and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for variable compute loads, though shared scheduling introduces potential execution variance under sustained maximum utilization. Combined with 320 GB of fast local NVMe storage, the instance is well matched for CI/CD compilation runners, static and dynamic web application hosting, build systems, microservices, and general backend caching services.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx42 is a compute-focused virtual server equipped with 8 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs operating at 2.0 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture and hosted via QEMU, the hardware package includes 320 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, modern AVX-512 vector support, and hardware cryptography extensions, without discrete GPUs. Empirical testing shows top-quartile single-core metrics, achieving a stress-ng single-core score of 2,991.79 and 14.1 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression, alongside average multi-core and memory subsystem throughput across PassMark, Geekbench, and Redis benchmarks. With balanced local storage density and shared compute resources, the cpx42 delivers qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded build environments, web serving, CI/CD pipelines, and application backends.
